chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, altogether from Al-Jamourani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Tameemi, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from his father, who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Treat the wagtails with goodness, meaning the swallows, for these are the friendliest of the birds of the people with the people'.
Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'And do you know what the wagtail (swallow) says when it passes by and sings? It says: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful'.
The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the Worlds
until he (peace be upon him and his family) recited the 'Mother of the Book' (Surah Al-Fatiha).
So when it comes the end of its singing, so she says, 'Wa La Zalleen' (the last words of Surah al-Fatiha).
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) extended his voice with it, 'Wa La Zalleen'.

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) say about the recitation of swallows?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to highlight the spiritual sensitivity of creation, where the swallow's song is interpreted as a literal recitation of Surah Al-Fatiha, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the ubiquity of divine praise in nature. The Prophet’s extension of his voice on 'wa lā al-dāllīn' underscores the significance of this phrase in liturgical practice and serves as a reminder of the bird's innate connection to human worship.
